scope: Five PMC full texts newly verified from the 2017-2025 discovery batch
basis: Compared the source title and abstract with the thesis scope. Only research directly addressing U.S.-China media/discourse competition or a clearly documented comparative communication context is retained as formal full text.

retained_material_ids.title: COVID-19 vaccines as a game-changing tool? A corpus-based study of vaccine communication in People's Daily and The New York Times
retained_material_ids.reason: Directly compares vaccine communication in People's Daily and The New York Times and discusses U.S.-China strategic rivalry.

pending_materials.title: Did the popularization of the Internet impact Chinese citizens’ attitude towards foreign countries? An empirical study based on two surveys
pending_materials.reason: Studies Chinese public attitudes and media channels but the reviewed title and abstract do not establish a direct U.S. or U.S.-China communication focus.

pending_materials.title: Worsening British views of China in 2020: evidence from public opinion, parliament, and the media
pending_materials.reason: Studies UK public opinion, parliament, and media; its comparative value to the U.S. case needs explicit researcher review before formal inclusion.

excluded_materials.title: Perspectives on Surrogacy in Chinese Social Media: A Content Analysis of Microblogs on Weibo
excluded_materials.reason: Concerns domestic social media debate about surrogacy and does not address U.S.-China discourse or communication competition.

excluded_materials.title: Housing safety and health academic and public opinion mining from 1945 to 2021: PRISMA, cluster analysis, and natural language processing approaches
excluded_materials.reason: Concerns housing safety and health research and public discussion, unrelated to the thesis topic.

evidence_policy: Excluded or pending full-text materials are removed from the formal materials table; original source evidence and candidate history are retained.
